topic: Maurya vs Gupta — comparison — mixed tiers
description: Compare Mauryan + Gupta — chronology, administration, religion, art

questions.stem: The MAURYAN empire and GUPTA empire are separated by approximately:
questions.explanation: MAURYAN EMPIRE: 322 BCE - 185 BCE (founded by Chandragupta Maurya; greatest = Ashoka). GUPTA EMPIRE: ~320 CE - 550 CE (founded by Chandragupta I; greatest = Chandragupta II Vikramaditya). Gap of ~500 years between fall of Mauryas + rise of Guptas — filled by SHUNGAS (185-73 BCE), KANVAS, SATAVAHANAS (south), KUSHANS (Kanishka, 1st-3rd c. CE), SAKAS, INDO-GREEKS. Coincidence of dates: 320s BC for Mauryan, 320s CE for Gupta — both 'Chandragupta'.

questions.stem: Both Mauryan + Gupta empires had their CAPITAL at:
questions.explanation: PATALIPUTRA (modern PATNA) — capital of multiple empires: NANDAS, MAURYAS, SHUNGAS, GUPTAS. Strategic position at confluence of Ganga + Son (also Punpun, Gandak) — major river trade hub. Greek ambassador MEGASTHENES (under Chandragupta Maurya) wrote 'INDIKA' describing Pataliputra in detail (~50 sq km, 64 gates, 570 towers — described as 'most magnificent city' of his time). Earlier called Pataligrama (a small village; according to Buddha's prophecy, would become great city). Decline: invasions, river course shifts.

questions.stem: Mauryan emperor ASHOKA's main religious patronage went to:
questions.explanation: ASHOKA (r. 268-232 BCE) — initially traditional Hindu / aggressive ruler. KALINGA WAR (261 BCE) — bloody victory horrified him → embraced BUDDHISM. Spread it through: ROCK + PILLAR EDICTS (across India, in Brahmi + Kharoshthi scripts; also Greek + Aramaic in Afghanistan); MISSIONS to Sri Lanka (son Mahindra + daughter Sanghamitra), Burma, Central Asia; THIRD BUDDHIST COUNCIL at Pataliputra (250 BCE, under Moggaliputta Tissa); state policy of DHAMMA (ethical code, non-violence, tolerance). His emblem (4-lion capital, Sarnath) = India's national emblem. Distractor 3: Chandragupta MAURYA (his grandfather) is said to have embraced JAINISM in old age, abdicating to die in Shravanabelagola.

questions.stem: GUPTA AGE is famously called the 'Golden Age of India' because of:

options.option_text: Discovery + use of pure gold mines

questions.explanation: GUPTA AGE (~320-550 CE) called GOLDEN AGE for: (1) LITERATURE — KALIDASA (Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsa), Sudraka (Mricchakatika), Vishakhadatta (Mudrarakshasa), Bharavi, Dandin. (2) SCIENCE — ARYABHATA (~499 CE; Aryabhatiya — π ≈ 3.1416, Earth rotates, sun's distance, value of zero); VARAHAMIHIRA (Brihat Samhita, astronomy + astrology); BRAHMAGUPTA (later, ~628 CE — quadratic eqs, zero). (3) MATHS — DECIMAL system + ZERO (became 'Hindu numerals' → 'Arabic numerals' in West). (4) ART — Ajanta + Ellora paintings (Ajanta cave 1, 17, 19 = Gupta period); Sarnath Buddha. (5) MEDICINE — SUSHRUTA SAMHITA (Charak earlier). Distractor 1: Mauryan empire was actually larger (Ashoka's reach > Guptas).

questions.stem: The MAURYAN administration was famous for which detailed treatise on statecraft?
questions.explanation: ARTHASHASTRA — comprehensive treatise on STATECRAFT, economics, military strategy, espionage, diplomacy, taxation, foreign policy. Written by KAUTILYA (also known as Chanakya / Vishnugupta) — Chandragupta Maurya's chief advisor (~4th c. BCE; rediscovered 1905). Themes: importance of dharma, importance of king's safety, MANDALA THEORY of foreign policy (concentric circle of ally / enemy), SPY networks, taxation. Often compared with Machiavelli's 'The Prince' (much earlier, more comprehensive). Contains the famous saying: 'an enemy of an enemy is a friend' (mandala).

questions.stem: Chinese pilgrim FA-HIEN (Faxian) visited India during the reign of which Gupta emperor?
questions.explanation: FA-HIEN / FAXIAN (Chinese Buddhist monk) — visited India ~399-414 CE, during reign of CHANDRAGUPTA II VIKRAMADITYA (r. 380-415 CE). Travelled to study Buddhist texts. Wrote 'FOGUOJI' (Records of Buddhist Kingdoms) — described Indian society, Buddhism, customs. Praised peaceful + prosperous life. Other Chinese visitors: HIUEN TSANG (Xuanzang) ~629-645 CE — Harsha's reign; I-TSING (Yijing) ~671-695 CE — Pala period (later, after Guptas).

questions.stem: Which empire had MEGASTHENES (Greek ambassador to Indian court) as a foreign visitor?
questions.explanation: MEGASTHENES — Greek envoy sent by SELEUCUS NICATOR (Alexander's general, founder of Seleucid empire) to the court of CHANDRAGUPTA MAURYA at Pataliputra (~302 BCE). Stayed several years. Wrote 'INDIKA' (now lost; survives in fragments quoted by later Greek writers — Strabo, Arrian, Diodorus). Described India's society, geography, government, army (~600,000 infantry + 30,000 cavalry + 9000 elephants — likely exaggerated). Famous descriptions: '7 castes' (his classification), Pataliputra's grandeur. Distractor 1 — Fa-Hien visited Gupta. Distractor 3 — Hiuen Tsang visited Harsha.
